items.text: REFERRED TO MENTAL HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES

items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to appointments and duties of the developmental disabilities advisory council and to the submission and posting of a statewide plan for services
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5060

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to appointments
and duties of the developmental disabilities advisory council and to
the submission and posting of a statewide plan for services

PURPOSE:

To ensure that the state is able to provide sufficient service
capacity and appropriate level of care to individuals with
developmental disabilities.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 Amends subdivision (a) of section 13.05 of the mental
hygiene law (MHL) by granting the temporary president of the senate
and the speaker of the assembly each five appointments of individuals
to serve as members of the Developmental Disabilities Advisory Council
(DDAC).

Section 1 also amends the opening paragraph of subdivision (c) of
section 13.05 of the MHL by requiring the DDAC, in cooperation with
the commissioner of the office for developmental disabilities (OPWDD)
to provide recommendations on issues related to the transition of the
OPWDD service delivery system into managed care.

Section 2 Amends paragraph three of subdivision (b) of section 5.07 of
the MHL by clarifying that the comprehensive plan developed by the
commissioner of OPWDD must be submitted annually to the Legislature no
later than January fifteenth.

Section 3 Provides the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

New York State continues to work towards compliance with the Olmstead
Plan by moving individuals out of institutional settings and into less
restrictive community based programs, while simultaneously assessing
the feasibility of transitioning the OPWDD service system into managed
care. While most individuals would agree that this is an appropriate
long term plan, there are serious concerns that the pace of this
transition is too rapid and the capacity to provide services in local
communities does not exist.  Additional trepidation has resulted from
what seems to be a lack of transparency regarding the current capacity
of OPWDD's service system; gaps in services across the state; and a
clear and precise plan which aims to provide appropriate levels of
care for individuals with disabilities and support for their families.

In response, the State Fiscal Year (SFY) 2015-2016 Enacted Budget
included an Omnibus reporting bill that provides the following
information to the Legislature on services for individuals with
disabilities: (1) Regional housing needs, the priority of such need,
and developing housing alternatives; 2)Integrated employment
opportunities, including alternative work settings; (3) Increasing
access to self-directed models of care; (4) Monitoring the


developmental center census reduction and types of community based
services provided to individuals leaving developmental centers; (5)
Examining the program design and fiscal model for managed care to
appropriately meet service needs; and (6) the implementation of the
front door policy, including improvements made in determining priority
residential placements and the process for individuals to seek access
for services.

This information will prove to be invaluable by assisting the
Legislature to address the service needs of individuals with
disabilities during this period of transition. Unfortunately, these
provisions will be repealed and be deemed expired on April 1st, 2016.
It is obvious to most that the transition of the OPWDD service system
into managed care, as well as the state's efforts to be in compliance
with the Olmstead Plan will not be complete. In reality, it will
likely be several more years before this plan will be successfully
implemented; therefore, the need to monitor, assess, and report on
such Implementation will need to be continued.

Section 13.05 of the Mental Hygiene Law has established the
Developmental Disability Advisory Council. The Council currently has
the authority to provide recommendations to the commissioner of OPWDD
regarding statewide priorities and goals for services for individuals
with developmental disabilities, as well as assist in the development
of OPWDD's statewide 5.07 comprehensive plan. This bill would support
the implementation of OPWDD's transformation plan by requiring the
council to provide recommendations in relation to the reporting
provisions enacted in the SFY 2015-2016 Budget, once those provisions
have expired and been repealed; and the Council's recommendations
would be also included in OPWDD's 5.07 plan.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is a new bill.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

Undetermined.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act would take effect immediately; provided, however, that the
amendments to subdivision (a) of section 13.05 of the MHL made by
section one of this act shall take effect upon the next succeeding
reappointment time period, or as vacancies occur, and provided,
further, that the amendments to the opening paragraph of subdivision
(c) of section 13.05 of the MHL made by section one of this act shall
take effect April 1, 2016.

summary: Relates to appointments and duties of the developmental disabilities advisory council and to the submission and posting of a statewide plan for services; changes the appointment process so the governor appoints 23 members and the temporary president of the senate and the speaker of the assembly appoint 5 each; includes specific issues the council can recommend action on; requires statewide plans be posted on websites and submitted to the legislature by January 15th of each year.
